sections.h2: Which Oldham County office sends the tax bill?
sections.html:
The Oldham County Sheriff's office prints and collects the bill, and the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) supplies the value it is based on. According to the sheriff's tax collection page, the office gathers money for the state, the county, the school districts and the city of Crestwood, plus 18 special districts. Bills go in the mail by the end of September, and the office line is 502-222-9501.

A value that looks off is a PVA matter, reachable at 502-222-9320. The printed bill itself explains the due dates, how to dodge penalties, and what to do when a mortgage servicer pays on the owner's behalf.

sections.h2: What sets Oldham County apart from the rest of Kentucky?
sections.html:
Oldham County sits in north central Kentucky as part of the Louisville metropolitan area, and Wikipedia's county profile calls it both the wealthiest and the best-educated county in the state. At 196 square miles it is the 13th smallest of Kentucky's counties, and the Ohio River forms its northern border with Indiana.

The legislature formed it in 1823 from pieces of Henry, Jefferson and Shelby counties. New towns grew up along the Louisville and Frankfort railroad in the 1850s. Interstate 71, finished in the early 1970s, linked the county to downtown Louisville and Jefferson County shopping, and the county has leaned suburban ever since. La Grange is the seat and largest city. Crestwood, Goshen, Pewee Valley, Prospect, Orchard Grass Hills and River Bluff are also cities, while Buckner and Westport are census-designated places.

Oldham County Schools runs North Oldham High School, Oldham County High School and South Oldham High School. Buyers often ask which of the three an address feeds.

sections.h2: How do the Oldham County numbers look?
sections.html:
Home values run well above the Kentucky norm. The table draws on Census Bureau QuickFacts, with survey figures covering 2020 to 2024.

sections.h2: When are Oldham County owners expected to pay?
sections.html:
The calendar is statewide. Under KRS 134.015, a bill paid in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount, the face amount applies through December 31, and penalties of 5 and then 10 percent follow in January and later.

  • Owners whose lender pays from escrow should confirm that the payment landed before the November 1 discount date.
  • A buyer who closes in the fall should have the title agent say which side covers the current bill.
  • A parcel inside Crestwood carries the city's levy on the same bill as the county's.

Because ownership on January 1 fixes who owes the year's tax, a seller who closes in spring still gets the bill and squares it with the buyer at the closing table.

sections.h2: How does an Oldham County owner argue against a valuation?
sections.html:
Call the PVA and request a conference. A statewide PVA appeal guide treats this as the required opening move. The owner states an opinion of value and supports it with sales of similar houses, a recent appraisal, repair quotes or rental income records.

When the conference ends without agreement, the owner files an appeal form with the Oldham County Clerk by the day after the inspection period closes. A local board of three residents hears the case. A loser at that level can go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, which wants the filing within 30 days of the mailed ruling. In a county with $393,100 homes, even a small cut in assessed value can matter, so preparing comparable sales from the same subdivision is worth the time.

sections.h2: What does the clerk do with unpaid Oldham County bills?
sections.html:
Unpaid bills leave the sheriff at the close of business on April 15 and land with the County Clerk. The Oldham County Clerk's delinquent tax page sends valuation questions back to the PVA and tax sale questions to the Department of Revenue.

The state's collection guide describes what follows: a recorded lien, interest at 1 percent monthly, notices from the county attorney, and a sale no sooner than 90 days after the transfer. If a private investor buys the certificate, the owner pays that investor. A seller with an open certificate should clear it from the proceeds at closing, and the clerk can quote the payoff.

sections.h2: What costs does an Oldham County seller face at closing?
sections.html:
Kentucky's transfer tax falls on the seller. The rate is 50 cents for every $500 of value, rounded up, and the clerk collects it with the deed (KRS 142.050). A $393,100 sale spans 787 blocks of $500, so the tax comes to $393.50. Deeds that correct an earlier deed, follow a foreclosure or pass between spouses are exempt.

  • The deed names the full price and both parties' mailing addresses, and it gives an address for the next tax bill.
  • A gift or nominal-price transfer needs a sworn statement of estimated market value.
  • Heirs file the personal representative's affidavit in each county where the estate holds land.

sections.h2: What is driving the Oldham County housing market?
sections.html:
Growth is steady. The county gained about 3,400 residents between April 2020 and July 2025, builders took out 276 permits in 2025, and 46.4 percent of adults aged 25 or older hold a bachelor's degree. Broadband reaches 95.4 percent of households, and the average worker spends 26.2 minutes getting to a job.

Those figures describe a county tied closely to the Louisville job market. At the 2020 census, 74.8 percent of residents lived in urban areas. Because the sheriff collects for 18 special districts in addition to one city, two houses a few miles apart can pay different totals. Ask the sheriff which districts appear on a given bill before comparing two listings.

faqs.q: Whom should I call about an Oldham County property value?
faqs.a: The PVA, at 502-222-9320. The sheriff's office only collects what the PVA's values produce.

faqs.q: When do Oldham County property tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: By the end of September, according to the sheriff's tax page. If yours has not come by early October, call the sheriff at 502-222-9501.

faqs.q: Is Crestwood's city tax billed separately?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff collects the Crestwood levy together with the county and district charges, so one payment covers them.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies to a median-priced Oldham County sale?
faqs.a: $393.50 on a $393,100 sale. The seller owes it, and the clerk collects it before recording the deed.

faqs.q: Can a house with a tax lien on it still be sold in Oldham County?
faqs.a: Yes. The payoff comes out of the sale proceeds at closing, and the County Clerk can give the title company a figure good through a stated date.
